clue.text: Children's author needs wheels to turn — to create another?

parts.note: C. S. Lewis, of Narnia fame, is another children's author
wheels is slang for a car
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A children's writer must turn a wheel to dream up a second writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points to a second children's writer, C. S. Lewis, whose surname leads the answer even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dodgson wrote the Alice books under this pen name, so he is a classic writer for children.

clue.text: Gatecrashing party not quite when expected, a beastly prince?

indicators.note: a gatecrasher pushes in uninvited, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

indicators.note: not quite means falling short of complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: on cue means at the expected moment

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher arrives at a party slightly off schedule, a royal behaving like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the phrase for on time. The lion is called king of beasts, so its young is a prince among beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is called king of the beasts, so its offspring is jokingly a prince among animals.

clue.text: With design incomplete, a tidy sum wasted — on this project?

definitions.text: With design incomplete, a tidy sum wasted — on this project?

indicators.note: incomplete means missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an emblem is a design or badge

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or squandered, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A building scheme with an unfinished design that squandered a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The rebuilt national football ground in London, opened in 2007, ran famously late and over budget, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: England's national football stadium in London was rebuilt late and over budget, a project that swallowed a fortune.

clue.text: Wipe out vegetation

definitions.meaning: to cancel or erase, as when a plan is called off
stunted trees and bushes covering dry ground

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel it, and scrub is also low brushwood covering rough land.

clue.text: Decline to accept upstanding investigators, so step down

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to abate is to decline or lessen

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the piece is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Refuse to admit honest detectives, so resign.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, to step down from it.

clue.text: Here, tries getting past red

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game where tries are scored
by means past, as in walking by

explanation.surface: In this spot, attempts are made to get beyond the colour red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here, tries' means the place where tries are scored: rugby union, RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a deep red colour, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Long, limp-sounding flower in the house

indicators.note: sounding says the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: lank hair is long, straight and limp
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A tall, drooping-looking bloom stands in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is a royal dynasty, the House of Lancaster, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster was an English royal house, the dynasty of Henry IV, V and VI.

clue.text: Make connection properly between containers in Kentish Town

indicators.note: between places the middle pieces inside the outer one

parts.note: tuns are large casks
to bridge is to make a connection
well means properly

explanation.surface: Connecting pipes correctly between tanks in a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a London district, but here it means a town in Kent: the spa town of Tunbridge Wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in the county of Kent, so it is a Kentish town.

clue.text: Bit of an academic achievement

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as in to some extent
a qualification awarded by a university

explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a step or extent, as in to a degree, and also a university qualification.

clue.text: Window won't open in shell

indicators.note: a word that won't open has lost its opening letter, so the D at its start goes

parts.note: a dormer is a window set into a sloping roof

explanation.surface: A window that refuses to open, set in some kind of shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a mollusc, the abalone of the Channel Islands, standing for the shell it lives in.
explanation.definitionFit: This Channel Islands shellfish, an abalone, is prized for its ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Security has to exist in securing device

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a denture is a dental plate held firmly in the mouth, a device fixed in place
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A guarantee of safety is said to lie in some kind of locking gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link word. A denture is a plate of false teeth held firmly in the mouth, which is why the clue calls it a securing device.
explanation.definitionFit: A debenture is a bond secured on a company's assets, so it is a kind of financial security.

clue.text: A bicycle is rubbish ——- nothing personal!

indicators.note: rubbish suggests something wrecked or useless, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a bicycle as junk, insisting it is not a personal remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing personal!' is a jokey definition: a celibate life has no personal relations of the intimate kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibacy means abstaining from sexual relations, humorously described as having nothing personal going on.

clue.text: A closely harmonising composer?

parts.note: a hairdresser shaves closely and his shop gives its name to close four-part harmony singing

explanation.definitionFit: A men's hairdresser gives close shaves, lends his name to close-harmony singing, and shares a surname with an American composer.

clue.text: Cry "pity about note" where you'll hear plenty of them!

definitions.text: where you'll hear plenty of them!

parts.note: to bay is to cry out like a hound

indicators.note: about means round, so one word goes either side of the other

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity, as in ruthless
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone cries out for pity over a single musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' in the definition refers back to the notes: the German town hosts the Wagner festival, where notes abound.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bavarian town stages the annual Wagner opera festival, a place full of music.

clue.text: One weedless, wild flower

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One garden free of weeds, and a wild flower in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white Alpine flower with woolly bracts.

clue.text: Seconds before one carrying child is hit

parts.note: a trike, a child's tricycle, is something that carries a child

explanation.surface: Just seconds before someone holding a child gets struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a hit or blow; to strike something is to hit it.

clue.text: Video programmed to go in order

indicators.note: to go in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class
set means programmed, as a timer is set

explanation.surface: A video recorder is programmed to switch on in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A video cassette is the tape box once used to record television, so a video.

clue.text: Flower part extracting oxygen from different one

indicators.note: extracting means pulling something out, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: another means a different one
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Part of a flower has its oxygen drawn out of a second specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen, a part of the bloom.

clue.text: Much sought-after element, wind in summer

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, the coveted element
a gust is a sudden burst of wind

explanation.surface: A precious metal and a breeze on a summer's day.
explanation.definitionFit: This month falls in the northern summer, between July and September.

clue.text: Old song "Loopy," with a capital L!

parts.note: loopy is slang for mad
Riga is the capital of Latvia
the letter L as printed

explanation.surface: An old tune called Loopy, written with a big letter L.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a capital L' looks like a note on spelling, but it supplies Riga, a capital city, followed by the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is an unaccompanied part-song of the Renaissance, an old kind of song.

clue.text: To a great (or to a great big) extent?

definitions.text: To a great (or to a great big) extent?

parts.words: To a great (or to a great big) extent
parts.note: read normally it means mostly; split, it is the word for great big plus the adverb ending meaning to an extent

explanation.definitionFit: Largely means mostly or to a great extent, and contains the word for great big.

clue.text: Drop fleece inside dress

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another

parts.note: a gown is a dress
to fleece or do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A fleece slipped off beneath a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down is to drop or fall, as a sinking ship or falling prices do.

clue.text: Having taken the two of us in, the illusionist one avoids

indicators.note: having taken something in is holding it inside, so this piece encloses another
completes the phrase having taken ... in, signalling one piece goes inside

parts.note: M. C. Escher, the Dutch artist famous for impossible-staircase optical illusions
we are the two of us

explanation.surface: The magician has let the pair of us in, and one of us keeps out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the illusionist' suggests a stage magician, but it is the artist Escher, known for optical illusions.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to avoid, so someone who eschews something is one who avoids it.

clue.text: Large mammal in river

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hip
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A big animal wallowing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in river' looks like where the animal lives, but 'in' gives HIP, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippo, short for hippopotamus, is one of the largest land mammals.

clue.text: Ghanaian currency partial to price discrimination

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ghana's money seems fond of charging different customers different prices.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedi is the monetary unit of Ghana.

clue.text: Reversal of positions that's most foolish

indicators.note: reversal says the word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: puts means positions, as a verb
id est, Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Swapping places around is the silliest move there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' gives the Latin id est in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid means foolish, so its superlative means the most foolish of all.

clue.text: When you're gone, you haven't one bean!

definitions.text: When you're gone, you haven't one
definitions.meaning: a dead person has no heartbeat to feel at the wrist
beans, peas and lentils are edible seeds of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the heartbeat felt at the wrist, and also a legume seed such as a bean or lentil.

clue.text: Song you must remember through the years?

definitions.meaning: the song from Casablanca opens with the line You must remember this

explanation.definitionFit: The Casablanca song's title is also an everyday phrase meaning as the years pass.
